name: snapshot
description: The page as an outline of its elements -- role, name, value, state -- each with a ref to act on it by, and the page's address, title and tabs. With `ref`: that element's part of the page only.

ref.description: only this element and what is inside it
the element's ref: e12 from a snapshot, or p1 that the user picked

expect.description: What this action relies on that the user could have changed: they may be using the page while you think and write this call. Each check runs in the page right before the action, which is done only if every one is true -- else you are told what is there now and what the user did. `js`: a JavaScript expression about the page as the user sees it (document, location, the elements -- not the page's own script variables), true if it is as this action needs; with `ref`, that element is `el`. It runs in the tab shown, or its `ref`'s; `tab` (its number, as `tabs` lists them): in that tab's page -- e.g. the one a `tabs` switch or close is for. E.g. [{"ref": "e7", "js": "el.innerText.includes('Invoice #4411')"}, {"js": "location.pathname === '/invoices'"}], or [{"tab": 3, "js": "location.hostname === 'mail.google.com'"}]

name: steps
description: Several actions in one call, done in order: each step a call of one of these tools, as you would make it alone -- {"tool": "type", "ref": "e3", "text": "Jane", "expect": [...]} -- its own `expect` run right before it, which may also check what the steps before it should have done (the field now holds the text typed). It stops at the first step not done: the steps after it are not run. `snapshot`: the page's snapshot after them, done or not.

snapshot.description: the page's snapshot after the steps
